articles.title: Streak broken! Mohammed Siraj's six-year run comes to an end as India drop him again
articles.summary: Mohammed Siraj's remarkable run of featuring in every full away Test series since his debut has finally come to an end, with India leaving the pacer out
articles.body: Mohammed Siraj's remarkable run of featuring in every full away Test series since his debut has finally come to an end, with India leaving the pacer out of their playing XI for the second Test against New Zealand in Christchurch.Since making his Test debut at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) in 2020, Siraj had never missed an entire away Test series. However, with the team management once again opting against his inclusion for the Christchurch Test, the India pacer will miss his first full away series.Siraj's omission has attracted considerable attention, particularly given his impressive record in the ongoing World Test Championship (WTC) cycle. The 32-year-old is India's leading wicket-taker in the current cycle, with 43 wickets from 11 matches.His absence comes after India's bowling attack struggled to force a result in the opening Test at Wellington. Despite putting New Zealand under pressure for large parts of the contest, India could not bowl out the hosts in their second innings, with the match eventually ending in a draw.Siraj had also been in impressive form, particularly in overseas conditions. He played a memorable role in India's dramatic six-run victory over England in the Oval Test last year. The pacer has also been effective in Asian conditions, claiming 21 wickets in seven Tests at an impressive average of 21.28, including a four-wicket haul.For the opening Test, India had gone in with Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj as their four specialist fast bowlers, with Washington Sundar providing an additional bowling option. The combination was retained for the second Test, with young pacer Gurnoor Brar replacing Prasidh Krishna and receiving his maiden Test cap.Siraj is not the only senior player to miss out, with Ravindra Jadeja also left out of the playing XI for the second consecutive Test. India have continued to back Washington Sundar.With the two-match series still level at 0-0, India will hope the new-look bowling combination delivers in Christchurch. For Siraj, however, the selection call brings an end to a remarkable streak that had lasted nearly six years.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Hard to believe': Ex-India cricketer questions Mohammed Siraj's continued omission from playing XI
articles.summary: Former India cricketer Mohammed Kaif has questioned the team management's decision to leave Mohammed Siraj out of the playing XI for the second Test
articles.body: Former India cricketer Mohammed Kaif has questioned the team management's decision to leave Mohammed Siraj out of the playing XI for the second Test against New Zealand, saying the senior pacer should be among the first names considered for India's overseas bowling attack.Siraj was once again overlooked for the Christchurch Test despite being India's highest wicket-taker in the ongoing World Test Championship (WTC) cycle, with 43 wickets in 11 matches.Reacting to the selection call, Kaif took to X and expressed his surprise at Siraj's continued absence, while also pointing to the praise the pacer has received from India's bowling coach Morne Morkel."Hard to believe as one of India's premier fast bowler Mohammed Siraj is dropped again. Siraj should be one of the first names considered in India's overseas Test bowling attack, alongside Bumrah. Interestingly, bowling coach Morne Morkel himself called Siraj a world-class bowler and said he was bowling well," Kaif posted on X.Siraj's omission has attracted attention, particularly after India's bowling attack failed to bowl out New Zealand in the series opener at Wellington, with the hosts managing to secure a draw despite being in a difficult position for large parts of the contest.While the team management has not explicitly explained the decision, captain Shubman Gill offered some insight into the selection thinking after the first Test."Sometimes you have to see which bowlers are in form, which bowlers are bowling the best," Gill said after the Wellington Test.Morkel, meanwhile, also spoke about his conversation with Siraj ahead of the second Test, suggesting that the team management wanted the pacer to take a step back and assess areas of improvement."The conversation I had with him was to say, ‘Listen, let's just step it back a little bit. Where are we at the moment, what do we need to improve, and where can we get better?,” Morkel said on Thursday, on the eve of the second Test.Siraj had also been in impressive form in overseas conditions. He played a memorable role in India's dramatic six-run victory over England in the Oval Test last year. The pacer has also claimed 21 wickets in seven Tests played in Asian conditions at an average of 21.28, including a four-wicket haul.For the series opener, India opted for Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj as their four specialist pacers, with Washington Sundar providing an additional bowling option. The combination was retained for the second Test, with young pacer Gurnoor Brar replacing Prasidh Krishna and receiving his maiden Test cap.Ravindra Jadeja has also been left out of the playing XI for the second consecutive Test, with India continuing to back Washington Sundar.With the two-match series still level at 0-0, India's decision to persist with the bowling combination while leaving out their leading wicket-taker in the ongoing WTC cycle remains a talking point.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'One bad day for us': Tilak Varma admits India A's bowling let them down after Sri Lanka A's stunning chase
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India A captain Tilak Varma admitted that his side's bowling failed to deliver when it mattered after a crushing eight-wicket defeat to Sri
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India A captain Tilak Varma admitted that his side's bowling failed to deliver when it mattered after a crushing eight-wicket defeat to Sri Lanka A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars semifinal on Thursday. Despite putting 317 on the board, India A were knocked out after Sri Lanka A chased down the target with 9.3 overs to spare, powered by centuries from openers Lasith Croospulle and Sineth Jayawardene.Calling it “one bad day” for his side, Tilak credited the Sri Lankan batters but acknowledged that India A would need to introspect on their bowling after failing to defend a challenging total.“Yeah, credit goes to them. Both the openers played really well. But at the same point again, I was trying all the bowlers, but one bad day for us. I couldn’t get any help. But it’s fine. One odd bad day, but credit goes to Sri Lankan batsmen,” Tilak said after the match.The India A skipper also felt that the batting unit had done well throughout the campaign, while identifying bowling as an area that needed attention.“If you see as a batting group, we have done really well. But I think in bowling, we’ll go into the dressing room or go back home and introspect things, and we’ll come back stronger,” he added.'We haven't executed': Tilak on India A's failed bowling plansIndia A had hoped that 317 would be enough to put Sri Lanka A under pressure, particularly with the pitch expected to slow down as the innings progressed. Tilak revealed that the plan was to keep the scoring rate in check during the first 15 overs and make batting more difficult later.“Yeah, I was telling my boys that initially the first 15 overs will be very crucial. If we restrict them to anything six per over, it will be very good for us. Later on, the wicket gets slightly slower side. That’s what we planned, but unfortunately we haven't executed,” he said.Tilak believed India A had a competitive total after recovering from a middle-order wobble, with Shahbaz Nadeem and Tanush Kotian adding valuable runs towards the end.“Honestly, we thought that around 320, 330 will be a good score on the board. But, you know, the wicket was slightly slow after the 20 overs. Initially, first 20 overs, it was nicely coming onto the bat. But after that, slightly slower side. Few balls were gripping and staying low. So, but there again, we got like three wickets back to back we got out. So after that, coming back to Tanush and Shahbaz, the way they played, and 318 (317) was good on the board,” he said.Sri Lanka A openers dismantle India A attackIndia A's plans unravelled almost immediately as Croospulle and Jayawardene made the most of early reprieves. Jayawardene hammered 105 off 70 balls, while Croospulle scored 116 off 107, the pair adding 174 for the opening wicket to take the game away from India.Nishan Madushka remained unbeaten on 58 and shared an unbroken 53-run stand with Pavan Rathnayake (31 not out) to complete the chase at 318 for two in 41.3 overs.Earlier, Abhishek Sharma's 78, Tilak's 53 and Sooryavanshi's 40 gave India A a flying start. But after the top order lost momentum, Nadeem's unbeaten 54 and his 73-run partnership with Kotian helped lift the total to 317 for eight.Tilak also highlighted the positives from the campaign, pointing to the contributions of debutants and the depth they brought to the side.“Yeah, it is really positive things. You know, there are so many youngsters who have first time playing, especially Shahbaz and Tanush. Tanush himself has debuted and also Shahbaz. You have seen he has handy bowling and also he can bat down the order. It’s really positive thing. And also Tanush, he’s also an allrounder coming back again,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: If Mohammed Siraj is world-class, why is he out? Morne Morkel backs pacer amid selection questions
articles.summary: Mohammed Siraj is going through a difficult phase and finds himself out of India’s playing XI even in conditions that suit his bowling style, but bowling
articles.body: Mohammed Siraj is going through a difficult phase and finds himself out of India’s playing XI even in conditions that suit his bowling style, but bowling coach Morne Morkel has no doubts about the pacer’s quality.Ahead of the second Test against New Zealand, Morkel threw his weight behind Siraj, stressing that selection was beyond the bowler’s control and that the immediate priority was to take stock of his game and find a way back.“For me, he is bowling well. He is a world-class bowler. Sometimes selection decisions are tough to take,” Morkel said.The former South Africa pacer revealed that his message to Siraj has been to simplify things rather than obsess over selection.“The conversation I had with him was: ‘Listen, let’s strip it back a little bit. Where are we at the moment? What do we need to improve and where can we get better?’”Morkel added that Siraj, as a senior member, also had a role to play even when not in the XI.“Selection is something we can’t really control. All we can control is putting our energy into the guys who are playing,” he said. “At the same time, he can take stock of his own game, where he is at and what is going to be his best path back into the team. That comes down to grit and taking responsibility.”But the bigger question is: should Siraj’s performances in Asian conditions be the yardstick for judging his suitability for New Zealand?Would the same principle be applied to a batter? Had Shubman Gill or Yashasvi Jaiswal endured three ducks across two Tests in Sri Lanka, would they have been dropped in New Zealand?The numbers make Siraj’s omission intriguing. Since his heroics in England, he has played seven Tests, all in the subcontinent, taking 21 wickets at 21.28 and a strike rate of 44.2, considerably better than his career strike rate of 51.Then there are the two Tests in Sri Lanka, which appear to have counted heavily against him.At Galle, Siraj returned 1/29 and 1/15 from nine overs in each innings. Fellow seamer Prasidh Krishna took 1/47 and 2/16. At the SSC, Siraj had 1/33 and 1/26, while Prasidh returned 3/52 and 1/57.Here’s the context, though.India enforced the follow-on at SSC after spending 89.4 overs in the field in Sri Lanka’s first innings.One criticism of Siraj in Sri Lanka was the drop in his pace. Didn’t India’s quicks, including the great Jasprit Bumrah, experience something similar on the sluggish Basin Reserve surface in Wellington?Interestingly, Morkel cautioned against viewing speed-gun readings in isolation.“I wouldn’t read too much into the speed gun from the last game because of the nature of the surface,” he said. “The data and the black-and-white facts showed that the wicket lost a lot of pace quite early in the Test.”The SSC surface, too, had lost pace as the Test progressed and was more conducive to spinners, but even they couldn’t succeed.For Morkel, the larger issue is India learning to operate better with the Kookaburra once its initial hardness and movement disappear.“My experience from playing 16 years with a Kookaburra ball is that you need to make that new ball count,” he said. “You need to get the ball in the right areas and sometimes be a bit braver with your lengths and lines, even if that means going for a few runs.”Morkel also defended Anshul Kamboj from criticism after Wellington, arguing that judging a fast bowler on pace and returns without factoring in the surface would be unfair.And therein lies the contradiction surrounding Siraj.If conditions must be factored in while assessing Kamboj at Wellington, doesn’t Siraj deserve similar allowance for his performances on unresponsive surfaces in Sri Lanka?Meanwhile, the tall and quick Gurnoor Brar is pushing for a Test debut, with Morkel admitting his pace and bounce could be well suited to New Zealand conditions.As India grapple with a new bowling combination, a bowler described as world-class is wondering whether he will figure in it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ | Standing up to 140kph: How wicketkeepers are turning an old tactic into an attacking weapon
articles.summary: From Alex Carey standing up to Scott Boland in the Ashes to Tom Blundell doing it against Matt Henry in England and at the Basin Reserve last week and
articles.body: From Alex Carey standing up to Scott Boland in the Ashes to Tom Blundell doing it against Matt Henry in England and at the Basin Reserve last week and Rishabh Pant employing the ploy in the first Test, wicketkeepers are increasingly prepared to stand up even when the ball is arriving at 130-140kph.Beyond the obvious courage required, the keeper is increasingly becoming a thief of the batter’s space.Former India wicketkeeper Chandrakant Pandit believes it is a response to how batting has evolved in the post-T20 era. “Today’s batters, even in Tests, have the courage to step out against pace. There is no fear about coming out of the crease to counter movement,” Pandit told TOI from Mohali, where he is coaching Madhya Pradesh in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy.“So the keeper standing up is basically an attempt to counter that and prevent the batter from advancing.”There is evidence that it works. Data from New Zealand’s 2026 series in England showed England averaging 25.36 against pace with Blundell back, but only 15.26 when he stood up.Henry explained why the Kiwis did it at the Basin for a long period of time. “The only mode of dismissal at the Basin was to bring the wickets into play and be prepared to look boring. Putting the ball outside off wasn’t going to help as there wasn’t a lot of carry.”India bowling coach Morne Morkel, though, remains unconvinced. “I’m old school. I like a bit of pace and bounce, balls carrying through to second and third slip, and getting your dismissals that way,” he said on Thursday.Pandit feels if a batter stands a yard outside his crease, he can alter the length at which the bowler wants to operate.“When the bowler alters his length, he can also compromise his swing,” he said. “If the wicketkeeper comes up, it puts the batter in two minds. He may want to play a delivery on the front foot, but with the keeper standing up, he might instead play it off the back foot.”That hesitation can bring bowled and lbw into play without the keeper ever touching the ball.At The Oval, Blundell stood up for most of Henry’s 24 overs despite the seamer operating around 135kph. All five wickets in Henry’s first-innings five-for came with Blundell up.For Pandit, that deserves admiration. “The wicketkeeper has to have a lot of courage to stand up at this sort of pace. It means he believes in his skills and is fearless.”Better protective equipment has helped. “You have helmets now. I don’t remember us wearing helmets while keeping, even on turning tracks or bad wickets. The quality of protective equipment is much better today. But equipment alone cannot give you courage. You still have to believe you can do it.”Pandit remembers Sunil Gavaskar once asking him to stand up to Raju Kulkarni in domestic cricket. “I started sweating,” he laughs. Gavaskar, he says, was employing some reverse psychology, possibly trying to suggest to the quick that he wasn’t bowling fast enough. Ramakant Desai would also ask Pandit to stand up in club cricket, hoping to create leg-side stumping opportunities off his inswingers.The tactic carries obvious risks: less reaction time and the possibility of conceding byes. But Pandit believes teams will accept the trade-off. “The idea is to disturb the batter. Tactically, you take that chance.”Learning the skill, however, requires sustained drills.“I would start with a tennis ball, hit with a racket from eight or 10 yards so the keeper can work on his reflexes,” he said. “The first thing is to get the fear out of his mind. Then progress to a hard ball with somebody throwing, and after that the bowling machine.”And repetition counts more than reputation.“No matter how good you are, you still need to practise. If Rishabh Pant is going to stand close to the stumps, he would definitely have practised it.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Deny until you die': Ben Stokes makes explosive remark on Sandpapergate controversy
articles.summary: Former England captain Ben Stokes has urged those involved in the renewed Sandpapergate controversy to bring the matter to a close, warning that the
articles.body: Former England captain Ben Stokes has urged those involved in the renewed Sandpapergate controversy to bring the matter to a close, warning that the continuing revelations are taking a toll on players, support staff and their families.Speaking at the launch of his podcast, That's Not Cricket, Stokes said the prolonged public debate was creating unnecessary stress and anxiety for people who had already been through a difficult episode.While calling for an end to the controversy, Stokes also held the Cricket Australia leadership of the time accountable for the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, saying those in charge "have a lot to answer for". He described the latest developments as a "deny until you die" saga and suggested that the full truth may not emerge anytime soon, given how deeply the issue has become embedded."For the sake of players, the staff, the management who were involved in this whole situation, for the sake of their families, for the sake of their friends, the best thing for it to do now would be for it just to stop," he said on his That's Not Cricket podcast.Stokes also drew a parallel with his own experience of being under intense media scrutiny, explaining how such situations can affect people beyond those directly involved."It’s affecting people who do not deserve to be affected by this. Because I’ve been through something like this when you are so heavily in the media for something, I’ve seen what it’s done to people who don’t deserve to be put through stress, put through anxiety," he added.However, Stokes was equally critical of Cricket Australia's leadership during the original scandal, questioning the way the episode had been handled and the continued uncertainty surrounding it.“Whoever was in charge of Cricket Australia at the time has a lot to answer for this. It’s got so deep into it...that it’s almost just like ‘deny until you die’ one way or the other. I’ve been in the dressing room for long enough to form my own very well-educated guess on what I think has happened, but I don’t think in the close future we're going to hear what truly happened because it’s just so deep," he noted.The Sandpapergate debate has resurfaced nearly eight years after the infamous ball-tampering incident during the 2018 Cape Town Test. Fresh claims by former Australia opener Usman Khawaja in his memoir have brought the episode back into the spotlight, with the cricketer alleging that the entire team was aware of the ball-tampering plan.Khawaja's account has reportedly divided opinion within the Australian cricket fraternity and prompted fresh scrutiny of the original investigation, particularly regarding how extensively the incident was examined.The discussion has since widened, with several current and former cricketers weighing in on Khawaja's claims. His suggestion that Cape Town was not the only Test in which Australia tampered with the ball has further fuelled the controversy.With fresh accounts continuing to emerge, Stokes believes the renewed debate is now taking a human toll on those connected to the episode and has called for the matter to finally be put to rest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tom Latham overtakes Brendon McCullum to enter New Zealand's top four in Test run charts
articles.summary: New Zealand captain Tom Latham added another milestone to his Test career on Friday, moving past Brendon McCullum to become the country's fourth-highest
articles.body: New Zealand captain Tom Latham added another milestone to his Test career on Friday, moving past Brendon McCullum to become the country's fourth-highest run-scorer in the longest format.Latham achieved the feat during the opening day's play of the second Test against India at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. The left-handed batter went past McCullum's tally of 6,453 runs, taking his career total to 6,454 in 174 innings across 97 Tests.McCullum represented New Zealand in 101 Tests between 2004 and 2016, accumulating 6,510 runs in 174 innings. Latham needed just four runs to move ahead of the former captain but had to wait after failing to score in either innings of the series opener at the Basin Reserve in Wellington.He finally got off the mark in Christchurch on the second ball he faced and moved to 4 runs off nine deliveries on the third ball of New Zealand's third over, crossing McCullum's mark in the process.Latham also brought up his 32nd Test half-century during the second Test, adding another significant achievement to his day.The New Zealand captain went on to score 59 off 128 deliveries, hitting six boundaries before Akash Deep brought his innings to an end in the 42nd over. The Indian pacer produced a superb delivery that angled in before holding its line outside off, drawing Latham forward in defence and inducing a fine outside edge. Rishabh Pant completed a straightforward catch behind the stumps to give India a much-needed breakthrough.Former New Zealand captain Kane Williamson remains at the top of the all-time list with 9,515 runs from 110 Tests. Williamson, who announced his retirement from Test cricket earlier this year, is followed by Ross Taylor (7,683) and Stephen Fleming (7,172).Most runs for New Zealand in TestsPlayerTime spanMatchesInningsRunsBest scoreAverage100s50s0sKane Williamson2010-20261101959,51525154.06333812Ross Taylor2007-20221121967,68329044.66193514Stephen Fleming1994-20081111897,172274*40.0694616Tom Latham2014-202697*174*6,510*264*38.75173217Brendon McCullum2004-20161011766,45330238.64123114Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: SMAT: Musheer Khan's 65 gives Mumbai sixth victory
articles.summary: Mumbai skipper Suryakumar Yadav endured his first failure of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy but Musheer Khan’s 65 off 40 balls and Atharva Ankolekar’s 3/17
articles.body: Mumbai skipper Suryakumar Yadav endured his first failure of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy but Musheer Khan’s 65 off 40 balls and Atharva Ankolekar’s 3/17 powered the defending champions to an 86-run win over Uttarakhand in Kolkata on Thursday.Mumbai, who had one match washed out, finished the league stage unbeaten with six wins in seven matches to top Elite Group D and enter the Super League stage, beginning in Nagpur on Nov. 30.Batting at No. 6, Suryakumar was bowled by Jagadeesha Suchith for one. However, Mumbai piled up a formidable total thanks to contributions from Musheer, opener Angkrish Raghuvanshi (51 off 34), Hardik Tamore (39 off 14) and Sarfaraz Khan (31 off 15).Uttarakhand slumped to 58/5 in their chase before Shashwat Dangwal (37 off 20) and Suchith (19) offered some resistance.Ankolekar, Maxwell Swaminathan (2/35) and Musheer (1/1) then shared six wickets to bowl them out for 123.The eight teams through to the Super League are Baroda and Rajasthan from Group A, Delhi and Punjab from Group B, Andhra and Kerala from Group C, and Mumbai and Vidarbha from Group D.Arya continues to fire in Delhi winFollowing his record-breaking 181 in the previous match, Delhi skipper Priyansh Arya struck an unbeaten 56 off 30 balls to guide his side to an eight-wicket win over Railways in Indore. Tejasvi Dahiya chipped in with an unbeaten 41 off 16 balls as Delhi chased down 123 in just 11.1 overs.Chahar’s 3/13 takes Rajasthan throughDeepak Chahar gave IPL franchises a timely reminder of his ability ahead of the Dec. 16 auction, claiming 3/13 in four overs to guide Rajasthan to a sixwicket win over Bengal at the Wankhede.Puducherry stun Madhya PradeshPuducherry edged out Madhya Pradesh by two wickets, chasing down 158 with two balls to spare.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ 2nd Test: 0 runs, 3 wickets! India bowlers produce stunning turnaround against New Zealand
articles.summary: India came roaring back with a superb spell of fast bowling in the second Test against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch.
articles.body: India came roaring back with a superb spell of fast bowling in the second Test against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. After creating several chances without success, the Indian bowlers finally found their rhythm and picked up three wickets in the space of three overs.The sudden burst put New Zealand on the back foot, with Shubman Gill's decisions paying off. Akash Deep was the star of the spell, taking two wickets, while Anshul Kamboj also made an important contribution.Akash Deep breaks the stand, Kamboj strikes nextIndia were looking for a breakthrough at the drinks break after New Zealand reached 106/1 at the end of 39 overs. The visitors had come close on several occasions but had little to show for their efforts.There were missed run-out opportunities, a DRS call that did not go their way and a few edges and top-edges that failed to bring wickets. The ball was still moving off the surface, but the Indian bowlers were unable to make the most of it.Akash Deep eventually gave India the much-needed breakthrough in the 42nd over by dismissing New Zealand captain Tom Latham. The left-hander had made 59 off 128 deliveries before a brilliant delivery ended his stay.Akash Deep bowled a good-length delivery outside off stump. The ball came in initially before holding its line, forcing Latham to play at it. He managed only a faint outside edge, which was safely collected by wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant.The dismissal lifted the Indian team's spirits after a frustrating period in which they had struggled to break through.India did not have to wait long for another wicket. In the following over, Anshul Kamboj sent Henry Nicholls back for 16 off 46 balls.Kamboj bowled a short delivery, prompting Nicholls to attempt a pull shot. The batter was early into the stroke and could only manage a top edge. Akash Deep made no mistake at long leg to complete the catch.Akash Deep then delivered another beauty to dismiss Rachin Ravindra for a duck and complete a remarkable spell for India.Coming from around the wicket, the pacer got the ball to move in with the angle before taking it away off the seam. Ravindra went forward to defend but edged it to Pant, who took his second catch of the spell.In the space of three overs, New Zealand had gone from 110/1 to 110/4, giving India a big opportunity to take control of the match.Tom Blundell survives multiple close callsEven after picking up three quick wickets, the Indian bowlers kept creating problems for the New Zealand batters. However, Tom Blundell managed to survive a series of close calls.In the 45th over, Kamboj produced a big inswinger that struck Blundell on the pads. India appealed loudly for LBW, but Gill decided not to take a review after consulting the bowler. The delivery appeared to be going down the leg side.Blundell had another close escape against Gurnoor Brar in the 47th over. The pacer bowled a delivery at 136 kmph that pitched on off stump before moving away sharply. It beat Blundell's outside edge and went just over the off bail.Bumrah then thought he had Blundell trapped in front in the 48th over. After a discussion with Gill, India decided to review the umpire's decision.The pacer bowled a delivery that came back in sharply and beat Blundell's inside edge before hitting him on the back thigh. However, the ball-tracking showed that the delivery was going over the middle stump.India lost another review, while Blundell survived yet another testing moment against the Indian pace attack.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ILT20: Sherfane Rutherford's explosive fifty powers MI Emirates to 36-run win over Abu Dhabi Knight Riders
articles.summary: MI Emirates registered their second win of ILT20 Season 5 after beating Abu Dhabi Knight Riders by 36 runs at the Zayed Cricket Stadium on Thursday.
articles.body: MI Emirates registered their second win of ILT20 Season 5 after beating Abu Dhabi Knight Riders by 36 runs at the Zayed Cricket Stadium on Thursday.Sherfane Rutherford produced a stunning batting display, scoring 51 off just 18 balls, while Nicholas Pooran remained unbeaten on 42 off 33 deliveries. Their efforts helped MI Emirates post a massive 207/4 in 20 overs.The bowlers then stepped up to restrict the Knight Riders to 171/7. Fazalhaq Farooqi and Zahoor Khan picked up two wickets each, while Rashid Khan kept things tight with figures of 1/13. Sunil Narine was the standout bowler for the Knight Riders, taking 1/11, including a maiden.Rutherford, Pooran power MI Emirates to 207After being asked to bat first, MI Emirates got off to a flying start. Openers Kusal Perera and Muhammad Waseem attacked the bowling and added 77 runs for the first wicket in 52 balls.Perera scored 33 off 23 balls, while Waseem contributed 41 off 37 deliveries. The opening pair helped MI Emirates reach 57 without loss in the powerplay.Sunil Narine provided the Knight Riders with their first breakthrough in the ninth over when he dismissed Perera, who was caught behind.Abdullah Tarakhail, making his ILT20 debut, then struck twice to bring his team back into the contest. The Afghanistan pacer removed Waseem and Tajinder Singh (10 off 8), leaving MI Emirates at 124/3.The scoring rate slowed down for a while, with MI Emirates managing just one run in the 17th over. However, Rutherford and Pooran changed the momentum with some powerful hitting.The pair collected 17 runs each in the 18th and 19th overs to take the score to 177/3.Rutherford then took the attack to Knight Riders captain Jason Holder in the final over. He smashed three consecutive sixes off the first three deliveries to bring up his half-century in just 17 balls. However, he was caught on the fourth delivery.Kieron Pollard joined Pooran in the middle and made an immediate impact, hitting two more sixes. He scored 12 off just two balls as MI Emirates finished with a massive 207/4.Holder had an expensive outing, conceding 62 runs in his four overs. The last three overs alone cost the Knight Riders 64 runs.Farooqi, Zahoor lead MI Emirates' bowling attackChasing 208, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders began aggressively and collected 17 runs from Farooqi's opening over.However, the MI Emirates pacer bounced back quickly. He bowled Andre Fletcher (16 off 12) in the third over before dismissing Gulbadin Naib (5 off 6) in the fifth. The Knight Riders were reduced to 50/2.Zahoor Khan then removed Finn Allen (26 off 21) in the eighth over to put further pressure on the home team.Alishan Sharafu and Moeen Ali tried to revive the chase with a 45-run partnership off 27 balls. Both batters scored 36 runs, but Rashid Khan broke the stand by bowling Sharafu in the 13th over.Zahoor returned to dismiss Moeen in the 16th over, making the chase even tougher for the Knight Riders.Sunil Narine (4 off 15) retired out on the final ball of the 17th over. Andre Russell (6 off 3) was then bowled by Chris Jordan in the 18th over.Jason Holder (14 off 8) and Tarakhail (11 off 7) added some late runs, but the Knight Riders could only manage 171/7 in their 20 overs.Player of the Match Sherfane Rutherford spoke about his conversations with Kieron Pollard and Nicholas Pooran during the innings."(Kieron) Pollard and I had a chat about how you have more time than you think, and Pooran and I spoke about taking it deep. We were looking at 179-180, but the last two overs changed the game. I enjoyed it a lot, and I didn't realise it was three sixes in a row. It was good of Pollard to come in and finish it off."Abu Dhabi Knight Riders captain Jason Holder admitted that his team did not play well enough and failed to finish the bowling innings strongly."We were outplayed and a little flat. We bounced back nicely in the middle phase of our bowling innings but lost it at the back end. It's about executing better with bat and ball, and we didn't take a couple of chances early. We are a lot better than what we showed today, and I'm not worried. We'll assess when we review the game, and I wouldn't change anything I did today."Brief scoresMI Emirates: 207/4 in 20 overs (Sherfane Rutherford 51, Nicholas Pooran 42*, Muhammad Waseem 41; Sunil Narine 1/11, Abdullah Tarakhail 2/44).Abu Dhabi Knight Riders: 171/7 in 20 overs (Alishan Sharafu 36, Moeen Ali 36, Finn Allen 26; Zahoor Khan 2/38, Fazalhaq Farooqi 2/43).Player of the Match: Sherfane Rutherford.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Yashasvi Jaiswal surpasses Sachin Tendulkar to create history with rare Test feat
articles.summary: Yashasvi Jaiswal achieved a rare milestone in Test cricket on Friday (November 27), becoming only the second player in the world to feature in each of his
articles.body: Yashasvi Jaiswal achieved a rare milestone in Test cricket on Friday (November 27), becoming only the second player in the world to feature in each of his first 33 Test matches at different venues.The India opener reached the landmark during the second Test against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. Since making his international debut in the longest format against the West Indies at Windsor Park in Roseau on July 12, 2023, Jaiswal has represented India in 33 Tests, with every appearance coming at a different ground.Former India batter Sanjay Manjrekar is the only other player to have achieved the feat, having played his first 33 Tests at 33 different venues. Legendary batter Sachin Tendulkar is next on the list, having featured in his first 32 Tests at separate grounds.Former India fast bowler Javagal Srinath and West Indies wicketkeeper-batter Denesh Ramdin complete the top five. Both played their first 24 Test matches at different venues for their respective countries.Most Tests at different venues from debutPlayerTime spanTeamVenuesSanjay Manjrekar1987-1994India33Yashasvi Jaiswal2023-2026India33Sachin Tendulkar1989-1994India32Javagal Srinath1991-1996India24Denesh Ramdin2005-2008West Indies24Jaiswal's 33 Test appearances have come across seven opposition teams. He has played 10 matches against England, five each against New Zealand and Australia, four apiece against the West Indies and South Africa, two each against Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, and one against Afghanistan.The 24-year-old will have an opportunity to move past Manjrekar and claim the outright record when India begin their five-Test Border-Gavaskar Trophy campaign against Australia in 2027.The opening Test of the series is scheduled to be played at the Vidarbha Cricket Association Stadium in Nagpur from January 21 to 25. Jaiswal has already made an appearance at the venue, having played his ODI debut against England there on February 6, 2025. However, he is yet to feature in a red-ball international at the ground.A place in India's playing XI for the Nagpur Test would take Jaiswal's streak to 34 matches at different venues. However, his run is unlikely to extend beyond that, as the remaining four Tests of the series are scheduled to be held in Chennai, Guwahati, Ranchi and Ahmedabad, where he has already played Test cricket.The other venues for the 2027 Border-Gavaskar Trophy are MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai, Barsapara Cricket Stadium in Guwahati, JSCA International Stadium Complex in Ranchi and Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad. Jaiswal has featured in a Test at each of these grounds, meaning an appearance in the Chennai match after the Nagpur opener would bring his streak to an end at 34.Meanwhile, India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bowl against New Zealand in the second Test, which began at Hagley Oval on Friday.India made one change to their playing XI, handing fast bowler Gurnoor Brar his Test debut in place of Prasidh Krishna. Jasprit Bumrah presented the debutant with his Test cap.New Zealand, meanwhile, opted to retain the same playing XI from the previous Test.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cricket Australia gives players six weeks to share accounts of 2018 ball-tampering scandal
articles.summary: Cricket Australia (CA) has made public the terms of reference for its independent forum examining the events surrounding the controversial 2018 South
articles.body: Cricket Australia (CA) has made public the terms of reference for its independent forum examining the events surrounding the controversial 2018 South Africa tour, which became infamous for the ball-tampering scandal. The six-week exercise will give players and support staff who were part of the tour an opportunity to share their experiences, although individual accounts will remain confidential and will not be made available to the CA Board.The board will instead receive a report summarising the key issues raised during the process, along with recommendations. The document will not include individual testimonies or any supporting material. CA has also committed to releasing the complete report, together with its response, within 30 days of receiving it.The independent exercise will be overseen by senior counsel Fiona McLeod AO SC, who will conduct private sessions with those willing to participate. The forum was announced following fresh revelations surrounding the 2018 scandal in Usman Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr.In the book, Khawaja claimed that awareness of the sandpaper plan extended beyond the three players who were sanctioned by CA. David Warner and Cameron Bancroft have supported parts of his account, while Pat Cummins and several other bowlers have maintained that they had no knowledge of the plan.The forum will examine Australia's ball-management practices during the 2017-18 season, the team's involvement in all four Tests of the South Africa tour, and the incident involving Bancroft during the third Test in Cape Town on March 24, 2018. It will also look into CA's subsequent investigation into the episode.However, the exercise is not intended to reopen the original investigation or establish individual responsibility for the incident.CA has extended invitations to all players and support staff who were part of the South Africa tour, along with the management officials and board directors who were associated with the organisation at the time. Participants will be able to share their accounts through face-to-face or online meetings with McLeod, submit written statements or provide relevant documents.Taking part in the process is voluntary, and those who choose to participate will be permitted to have a support person or legal representative present.The terms of reference also lay down safeguards to protect the confidentiality of participants. Information shared by one individual cannot be attributed to them when seeking clarification from another participant unless they provide consent. Those involved will be informed about who can access their submissions and will have the opportunity to verify their own accounts for accuracy.In addition, the forum will be given access to the 2018 Culture and Governance Review of Australian Cricket conducted by The Ethics Centre, along with other relevant records and documents it considers necessary.CA Chair David Boon said the organisation was grateful to McLeod for agreeing to lead the initiative, which has been designed to provide a platform for everyone involved in the tour to share their experiences.“We’re grateful to Fiona McLeod AO SC for agreeing to lead the Independent Forum which has been designed to give voice to all the players and staff on the 2018 Test tour of South Africa," Boon said.“This is an opportunity to provide their accounts in a safe environment and to provide the CA Board with relevant information including about the events of that tour and resultant investigation.“We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority.“This forum is the best opportunity for people to speak and be heard, and for CA to listen and learn.“Publishing the report in full is part of our commitment to transparency, and to be open with cricket fans about what we learn.“It is also very important to understand that it will not seek to sanction or recriminate.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Akash Deep sizzles, Jasprit Bumrah struggles as New Zealand frustrate India on Day 1
articles.summary: CHRISTCHURCH: Twenty-two balls, three wickets and no addition to the scoreboard.
articles.body: CHRISTCHURCH: Twenty-two balls, three wickets and no addition to the scoreboard. The passage of play injected life back into India's bowling, and it was that man Akash Deep again. With the old ball, he found the right length for this surface, which still had enough bite to keep the bowlers interested. There was no magic formula for the Hagley Oval strip, and attacking the stumps while making the batter play was always going to test the batters."Pitch was fresh. The first session had more moisture, so edges didn't carry. We bowled in better areas in the second session and it worked. Pitch will get better if the sun remains out," he told reporters after the end of Day 1."The plan was to make the batter play, it was self-realisation. I wanted to make the batter play 90 per cent of the times. Ball was moving a lot in the first session," he added.After making the new ball talk and finding Tom Latham's edge (which KL Rahul grassed in the slips), Akash made the subtle adjustment to negate the extra bounce by going a touch fuller. The around-the-wicket angle against left-handers further planted seeds of doubt in the batters, who had no option but to play the line and get undone by enough movement off the pitch.Tom Latham was the first to fall to the plan, Rachin Ravindra followed in the next over during his spell, and an Anshul Kamboj breakthrough in between reduced the hosts from 110/1 to 110/4. In the space of 16 deliveries, three batters were back in the hut, and the relentlessness of the two fast bowlers paid off after they toiled hard in the first session.Akash, India's most threatening bowler on the day, bowled seven overs with decent pace. The figures read 7-4-7-2, and he could easily have taken a couple more wickets. He didn't get carried away by the bounce off the Day 1 strip and just stuck to the basics: hitting the same spot and subtly using the width of the crease to play with angles. Most importantly, he intended to make the batter play, which was key on a surface that had less grass compared to what we saw at the Basin Reserve in Wellington earlier this week."Overall, a good day, but we could have done better. We were discussing yesterday that this pitch is better than Basin Reserve," Akash said.From the other end, during different periods of play, debutant Gurnoor Brar bowled with pace and made effective use of the short ball. Anshul Kamboj sprayed it around with the new ball, but his spell with Akash after lunch put the hosts under pressure.Jasprit Bumrah was practising that run-up in practice also. Jasprit Bumrah hai wo, kuch soch ke hi kar rahe hoge (He's Jasprit Bumrah, after all. He must be doing it after giving it some thought).Introduced late into the attack, Washington Sundar got rid of dangerman Daryl Mitchell for 31, but another lower-order partnership, between Tom Blundell and Glenn Phillips, frustrated the visitors, who started playing the waiting game for the second new ball. Shubman Gill turned to his most successful bowler of the day, Akash, and Bumrah for the first crack with the red cherry, but New Zealand did well to negate that period.At stumps, Blundell and Phillips remained unbeaten, with the scoreboard reading 246/5.Bumrah strugglesHowever, it was Jasprit Bumrah's performance that will give India's management a thing or two to think about. Bumrah, the ace in the pack, had a rather underwhelming day, where he went past the bat, found some edges but returned wicketless. It has been over 200 balls since he last picked up a wicket in the series. He used an unusual run-up and load-up during his spell after Tea; it wasn't the usual way he held the ball, and his hands weren't in the position we've seen for over a decade now."Jasprit Bumrah was practising that run-up in practice also. Jasprit Bumrah hai wo, kuch soch ke hi kar rahe hoge (He's Jasprit Bumrah, after all. He must be doing it after giving it some thought)."The speed gun flirted around the 130 kph mark, and there was visible frustration with his trademark kick to the surface every time he went past the bat. Maybe it wasn't his day, but he was far from the menacing best we have seen in the past. Since the first over of the second New Zealand innings at the Basin, where he dismissed Tom Latham for a duck off the second delivery, the fast bowler has been searching for a wicket.Brief ScoresNew Zealand: 246/5 after 85 overs (Tom Blundell 53 batting, Tom Latham 59; Akash Deep 2/52)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ 2nd Test: Why is Jasprit Bumrah using a different run-up? Akash Deep has an answer
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Jasprit Bumrah's latest change in run-up caught attention on the opening day of the second Test against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Jasprit Bumrah's latest change in run-up caught attention on the opening day of the second Test against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Friday. The Indian pacer was seen using a different approach while running in. Bumrah, who remained wicketless on Day 1, was brought into the attack for a brief spell just before Tea, after Anshul Kamboj and Akash Deep had struck for India.While bowling to Tom Blundell, Bumrah appeared to change his usual routine. He was seen carrying the ball in one hand during his run-up instead of holding it with both hands, as he generally does.The unusual approach caught attention, and Akash Deep was asked about Bumrah's change during the post-match press conference."Woh practice match ke pehle bhi practice kar rahe the woh is tarah ki bowling ka. Toh ho sakta unke dimaag mein kuch planning hoga. Toh isliye karne honge. Jasprit Bumrah hai wo, kuch soch ke hi kar rahe hoge," Akash said.Akash Deep leads India's fightbackAkash Deep emerged as India's most impressive bowler on the opening day, picking up two key wickets after lunch. New Zealand ended the day at 246/5 after 85 overs, following a contest in which both teams had their share of success.New Zealand got off to a solid start, with Tom Latham (59) and Devon Conway (31) putting together 77 runs for the first wicket. India finally broke through on the last ball before lunch when debutant Gurnoor Brar (1/52) picked up his maiden Test wicket.Akash (2/52), who returned to international cricket after a lengthy break due to a lower back stress injury, then made an impact with two important strikes. He sent back the well-set Latham and Rachin Ravindra (0), with wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant completing both catches. Anshul Kamboj (1/56) also chipped in by dismissing Henry Nicholls (16). New Zealand, who were 77 without loss, suddenly found themselves struggling at 110/4.The hosts needed a partnership to steady their innings, and Tom Blundell provided it. He scored an unbeaten 53 off 117 balls and shared 74 runs with Daryl Mitchell (31). Washington Sundar (1/36) ended their stand when Dhruv Jurel caught Mitchell at leg-slip.Blundell was still at the crease at stumps, alongside Glenn Phillips, who was unbeaten on 36 off 64 balls. The duo added 62 runs for the sixth wicket without being separated, helping New Zealand finish the day on 246/5.Akash Deep on the pitch and India's plansAkash also shared his assessment of the pitch and explained how India approached their bowling. He said the moisture on the surface in the first session meant that edges were not carrying, while the bowlers found better conditions after lunch."Pitch was fresh. The first session had more moisture so edges didn’t carry. We bowled in better areas in second session and it worked. Pitch will get better if the sun remains out."Plan was to make the batter play, it was self realisation. I wanted to make batter play 90% of times. Ball was moving a lot in the first session."Overall good day, but we could have done better. We were discussing yesterday that this pitch is better than Basin Reserve. When ball gets old, it gets tougher for bowlers because we need to control flow of runs also. Its a way in these conditions."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Harry Brook wins the toss, England bowls first against Australia in 3rd cricket T20
articles.summary: BRISBANE, Australia (AP) — England skipper Harry Brook won the toss and sent Australia in to bat Friday as he bid to chase a target and a second consecutive...
articles.body:
BRISBANE, Australia (AP) — England skipper Harry Brook won the toss and sent Australia in to bat Friday as he bid to chase a target and a second consecutive victory in the five-game Twenty20 international cricket series.

England trounced Australia by eight wickets in the second game to level the series after Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt combined for a 151-run opening stand that set the visitors up to chase down a target of 185 in 14 overs at the Gold Coast earlier in the week.

England retained the same lineup. Australia made two changes, recalling paceman Billy Stanlake and allrounder Mitchell Owen for the match at the Gabba.

Australia beat England by three wickets in the series-opener at Melbourne.

The series will continue with a game in Sydney on Sunday and conclude in Canberra on Wednesday.

England won the preceding series of three one-day internationals 2-1, including a 97-run victory in the decider at Hobart.

Australia: Mitchell Marsh (captain), Jake Fraser-McGurk, Sam Harper, Nikhil Chaudhary, Tim David, Joel Davies, Mitchell Owen, Ben Dwarshuis, Adam Zampa, Riley Meredith, Billy Stanlake.

England: Phil Salt, Aneurin Donald, Harry Brook (captain), Tom Banton, James Coles, Sam Curran, Jordan Cox, Liam Dawson, Jamie Overton, Adil Rashid, Henry Crocombe.
